concerns.text: Task T026 (Implement permutation test generator) is marked [X] (complete) but is listed AFTER T027 (KS calculation) and T028 (QQ-plots). T027 and T028 explicitly require the permutation reference generated by T026. This violates the 'Producer before Consumer' rule; T026 must precede T027/T028.

Task T017 (Store full p-value trajectories) is marked [ ] (incomplete) but is a hard dependency for T026 (Permutation test generator) and T027 (KS calculation) which require the trajectory data to compute the Gold Standard reference. The current order implies T026 can run without T017, creating a semantic blocking violation.

Task T016 (Write data/synthetic/{seed}.json) is marked [ ] (incomplete) but T015 (Parameter sweep) and T022 (Integrate with generate_data) depend on the existence of these files to function. The task list implies T015 can run without T016, violating the data-flow dependency where the sweep orchestrator must write artifacts before downstream consumers can read them.

Task T004.5 (Define error code ERR_HIGH_DIMENSIONAL_INSTABILITY) is marked [ ] (incomplete) but is explicitly 'required by T004' (Implement covariance regularization) and 'referenced by T007'. T004 and T007 are marked [X] (complete). A task cannot be complete if it depends on an incomplete prerequisite error code definition.

Task T017.1 (Worst-case dataset) and T022.1 (Messiness visualizer) are marked [ ] (incomplete) but depend on T017 (Trajectory storage) which is also incomplete. While the dependency chain is logically sound, the grouping of these 'Feynman' tasks within the US1/US2 blocks without a clear 'Analysis' sub-phase makes the dependency on T017 less explicit in the visual flow.
